lists.intro:
If you didn’t grow up with a gray box connected to a tube TV via an RF adapter, you missed the era where games were actually finished at launch. 

Most of these "modern classics" wouldn't survive five minutes in 1988. 

Here is the definitive, no-filler Top 10 for the NES.
lists.outro:
The NES wasn't just a console, it was the standard. 

We didn't have patches, we didn't have DLC, and we didn't have "narrative-driven" walking simulators. 

We had 8 bits of pure, unfiltered gameplay. Every modern "masterpiece" is just standing on the shoulders of these giants.
lists.heading: Top 10 NES games

items.name: Super Mario Bros. 3
items.reason: The greatest game ever made. Not just on the NES, but of all time.
items.more:
The world map, the suits, and the sheer volume of secrets changed the industry forever. 

If you think any other game deserves this spot, you’re just trying to be different for the sake of it.

items.name: Adventures of Lolo
items.reason: Real gamers appreciate a puzzle. Lolo proves that you don't need a gun or a sword to have a "hardcore" experience.
items.more:
It’s a relentless logic trap that makes you feel like a genius for five seconds before the next room humbles you again. 

HAL Laboratory at its absolute finest.

items.name: Conquest of the Crystal Palace
items.reason: This is the best game you never played.
items.more:
It combines platforming with an actual shop system and a dog companion that actually helps you. 

The visuals were years ahead of 1990, and the difficulty curve is exactly how games should be balanced.

items.name: Contra
items.reason: The Konami Code is for people who can't handle a real challenge.
items.more:
Playing Contra with the standard three lives is the only way to experience the pure adrenaline of the jungle. 

It’s the peak of 8-bit action, and nothing in the last thirty years has topped the feel of the Spread gun.

items.name: Adventure Island
items.reason: Hudson Soft took the Wonder Boy formula and made it a punishing test of endurance.
items.more:
Managing your hunger meter while dodging snails is more stressful than any modern survival horror game. 

It’s colorful, bright, and will absolutely break your spirit.

items.name: Double Dragon II: The Revenge
items.reason: The controls are polarizing because they require a brain.
items.more:
Having buttons mapped to the "left" and "right" attacks instead of "punch" and "kick" is brilliant design. 

The cyclone kick is the most rewarding move in the beat-em-up genre, period.

items.name: X-Men
items.reason: Unfair? Yes.
items.more:
Chaotic? Absolutely. 

But LJN’s X-Men is better than the "hidden gem" YouTubers want you to believe. 

If you couldn't beat it, you just didn't understand the character swap mechanic. 

It’s a brutal, unforgiving gauntlet that rewards persistence over luck.

items.name: Duck Hunt
items.reason: The Zapper is the greatest peripheral ever made, and this game is the ultimate test of reflex.
items.more:
We all tried to shoot that laughing dog, but the real tension was hitting those clay pigeons on Round 15.

It’s pure, tactile arcade energy that modern VR still can't replicate.

items.name: Super Mario Bros. 2
items.reason: Stop calling it a "reskin" of Doki Doki Panic. This is the most experimental and creative Mario title in the entire 8-bit library.
items.more: Picking up enemies and throwing them is more satisfying than jumping on heads, and playing as Princess Peach was the original "easy mode" before it was cool.

items.name: Popeye
items.reason: Most arcade ports on the NES were compromised, but Popeye is pixel-perfect.
items.more:
It’s a masterclass in high-score chasing that requires more strategy than half the "open world" games released today. 

If you can't appreciate the perfection of the spinach mechanic, you aren't a real gamer.

lists.intro:
Every SNES top 10 list on the internet is identical. People just parrot Chrono Trigger and EarthBound because it is the safe, regurgitated internet consensus.

The 16-bit era was not about reading dialogue boxes for 80 hours. It was about rented cartridges, arcade ports, and raw muscle memory.

Here is the actual Top 10 best Super Nintendo games.

Top 10🧵⤵️
lists.outro:
The defining games of the 16-bit era didn't need sprawling maps or eighty-hour save files. 

They were built on raw mechanics, zero forgiveness, and the pressure of returning a cartridge by Sunday night. 

If your top 10 list is entirely made up of RPGs, you didn't actually play the SNES. You just read it.
lists.heading: Top 10 SNES games

items.name: Super Mario World
items.reason: The ultimate pack-in cartridge. It didn't waste your time with sprawling open worlds or cinematic tutorials.
items.more:
You turned on the console and were immediately playing the game. 

Thirty-five years later, the physics are strictly muscle memory.

items.name: Street Fighter 2
items.reason: This was the exact moment the arcade effectively moved into the living room.
items.more:
It was a flawless translation of the biggest cultural phenomenon on the planet. You didn't have to stack quarters on a cabinet anymore. 

The mechanics were so perfectly balanced that 'loser passes the controller' became the undisputed law of the house for an entire generation.

items.name: NBA Jam TE
items.reason: Midway forced a massive arcade cabinet into a plastic cartridge and ended friendships.
items.more: Hearing the SNES sound chip actually scream "Boomshakalaka!" or "He's on fire!" while you shoved your friend to the floor and shattered the glass backboard was the absolute peak of 90s competitive friction.

items.name: Yoshi's Island
items.reason: The Super FX 2 chip pushed the hardware until it almost broke, but the real achievement is the art design.
items.more:
Nintendo disguised one of the most mechanically demanding platformers ever made behind a flawless hand-drawn pastel coloring book aesthetic. 

It abandoned the standard run and jump blueprint for massive vertical exploration and exact egg throwing physics.

items.name: Batman Returns
items.reason: The Genesis version gets all the attention, but this beat 'em up is significantly meaner.
items.more:
Grabbing two clowns by the skull and physically smashing them into the concrete background never gets old. 

You actually feel the physical weight of the combat.

items.name: Super Mario Kart
items.reason: This practically invented the kart racing genre and immediately destroyed friendships.
items.more: It is brutally cheap, the rubber band AI is completely out of control, and hitting a perfectly timed green shell on Rainbow Road is still the most satisfying feeling on the system.

items.name: Captain America and the Avengers
items.reason: A Data East arcade port held together by duct tape.
items.more:
The audio compression is laughable and the hitboxes make zero sense. 

But frantically mashing buttons while the console struggles to process Iron Man screaming is the exact definition of couch co-op.

items.name: Tiny Toon Adventures Buster Busts Loose!
items.reason: Konami in the 90s was untouchable.
items.more:
They took a cartoon license and gave it the exact same mechanical precision as Castlevania. 

That football level is notoriously harder than it has any right to be. Pure linear platforming perfection.

items.name: Spiderman Venom Maximum Carnage
items.reason: LJN usually made unplayable garbage. They accidentally made a masterpiece here.
items.more: It actively hated the player, but grinding through the brutal difficulty and comic book cutscenes was an absolute staple of weekend Blockbuster rentals.

items.name: Michael Jordan Chaos in the Windy City
items.reason: Nobody talks about this one because the premise is completely insane.
items.more:
EA built a custom engine just to let you throw basketballs at mutant eyeballs. 

It sounds absurd, but the hit detection is incredibly tight and the difficulty is violently unforgiving.

earlier.intro:
Burn every other "Best of" list you’ve ever read. They are boring. They are objectively wrong.

This is the definitive, undisputed, personally validated Top 10 Super Nintendo games of all time.

Pure 16-bit adrenaline on a cartridge. Let the arguments begin.🧵
earlier.outro:
That’s the list.

I know Zelda and Chrono Trigger aren't there. I know Shaq Fu is.

I’m not changing it. You played what you owned, and I owned a fighting game starring a basketball player.

Post your Top 10 below.

items.name: Super Mario All-Stars + Super Mario World
items.reason: THE GOD CARTRIDGE.
items.more: The single greatest value proposition in the history of entertainment. The entire NES Mario legacy upgraded to 16-bit, PLUS the best launch title ever made. If you only owned this one game, you won the generation.

items.name: Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island
items.reason: A crayon-drawn miracle. Nintendo took the perfect Mario formula and somehow made it more charming, more challenging, and more beautiful. It hasn't aged a single day in 30 years. Absolute platforming perfection.

items.name: Street Fighter II
items.reason: The Alpha and the Omega. We literally sanded our fingerprints off playing this. We sacrificed layers of skin to the D-Pad gods just to throw a Sonic Boom.
items.more: This wasn't a game; it was a religion. It destroyed thumbs. It shattered controllers. It is the raw DNA of violence.

items.name: RoboCop vs. The Terminator
items.reason: You didn't play this game; you survived it.
items.more:
RoboCop moved like a tank. He felt heavy. The enemies were bullet sponges that shattered into scrap metal when you finally dropped them.

It was a constant, industrial grind of plasma and explosions. No finesse. No dodging. Just holding the fire button down and walking forward until everything on screen was dead.

items.name: Michael Jordan: Chaos in the Windy City
items.reason: The deepest cut on the list. The GOAT fighting robot spiders in the Chicago sewers using magical basketballs while saving fellow NBA players. It is peak 90s insanity.
items.more: If you missed this weird, wonderful fever dream, your childhood was incomplete.

items.name: Star Fox
items.reason: "DO A BARREL ROLL!"
items.more:
The Super FX chip wasn't hardware; it was alien technology welded into a plastic cart. We were playing a 3D space opera on a 2D system.

It looked like folded paper, it sounded like gibberish robots, and it played like a dream. If you didn't instinctively hit L or R when the screen flashed red, you didn't survive.

items.name: Super Mario Kart
items.reason: The CPU cheated. We all know it. Bowser had infinite fireballs. Mario popped a Star the second you passed him. It was completely unfair.
items.more:
But the driving was pure. You didn't just steer; you hopped. You had to rhythmically smash that shoulder button to drift around Ghost Valley without hitting the void.

Hitting a moving target with a Green Shell in this game is still the hardest shot in gaming history.

items.name: NBA Jam Tournament Edition
items.reason: "BOOMSHAKALAKA!"
items.more:
You can hear that text.

This game was 50% basketball and 50% soundboard. The announcer was screaming, the net was sizzling, and the crowd was losing its mind.

There were no fouls. There was just the Turbo button and the race to get "On Fire" so you could goaltend without consequence. The loudest game on the SNES.

items.name: Shaq Fu
items.reason: YES. I SAID IT. Put down your pitchforks. This game is a misunderstood masterpiece of bizarre 90s celebrity culture. Shaq fighting mummies in another dimension? It makes no sense and that's why it RULES. I will defend this cartridge with my life.

items.name: Ken Griffey Jr. Presents Major League Baseball
items.reason: The coolest athlete on the planet got the coolest game on the system.
items.more:
Before this, baseball games were tiny sprites viewed from space. Here, the camera was right behind the plate. You could actually read the pitch.

Striking out wasn't just a failure; it was a performance. Watching your player snap the bat over his knee in anger is still the best animation on the SNES.

lists.intro:
"Genesis does what Nintendon't" wasn't just a marketing slogan. It was an objective fact.

While Nintendo was busy sanitizing its ecosystem, Sega was building hardware exclusively for raw speed and unapologetic arcade violence.

If your 16-bit collection doesn't reflect that, you bought the wrong console.

These are the 10 best Sega Genesis titles.🧵⬇️
lists.outro:
People constantly debate the best Genesis games by just repeating the same predictable titles we all played for five minutes at a friend's house.

The games that actually define the console are the ones built on raw arcade friction, punishing momentum, and the absolute requirement to master the mechanics.

These ten cartridges aren't just a nostalgic ranking. They are the definitive reason the Sega hardware existed in the first place.
lists.heading: Top 10 Sega Genesis games

items.name: Sonic the Hedgehog 2
items.reason: The absolute ceiling of 16-bit speed and level design.
items.more: Everything that came after this was just a desperate attempt to recreate it.

items.name: Mortal Kombat II
items.reason: The definitive console port.
items.more: Nintendo sanitized their hardware, but the Genesis layout made the arcade violence immediate, raw, and exact.

items.name: RoboCop Versus The Terminator
items.reason: Peak physical media.
items.more: The sheer volume of on screen carnage and explosion animations has never been properly replicated in sanitized modern shooters.

items.name: X-Men
items.reason: The soundtrack alone justifies owning the physical cartridge.
items.more: Surviving the later stages required mechanical perfection. Modern developers are terrified of frustrating the player like this.

items.name: ESWAT: City Under Siege
items.reason: Stripped down arcade shooting.
items.more: Starting as a standard beat cop and earning the cyber suit through pure survival is a masterclass in earned power scaling.

items.name: Judge Dredd
items.reason: The Sega hardware was perfectly optimized for this aesthetic.
items.more: It is gritty, unforgiving, and forces you to rely on precise weapon management just to survive.

items.name: Adventures of Batman & Robin
items.reason: Pure punishing side-scrolling chaos.
items.more: The Jesper Kyd soundtrack pushes the audio chip to its mechanical limit. The brutal difficulty curve makes modern titles look like tutorials.

items.name: Batman: Revenge of the Joker
items.reason: A technical masterpiece that pushed the Genesis hardware to its absolute breaking point.
items.more: The graphics rival early 32-bit games and the difficulty is unapologetically brutal.

items.name: Altered Beast
items.reason: The ultimate launch-window statement piece.
items.more: It didn't rely on complex strategy. It was built on pure, heavy arcade friction, immediate power scaling, and unapologetic 16-bit body horror.

items.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Hyperstone Heist
items.reason: Nintendo fans obsess over Turtles in Time.
items.more: The reality is Hyperstone Heist plays significantly faster, has more aggressive enemy AI, and requires actual reflexes instead of just corner trapping.

lists.intro:
My top 10 N64 games. And Goldeneye isn't in the top three.

It's at 5. Four games beat it and I'll defend every one.

Most "Top 10" lists are the same four Nintendo first-party titles everyone copied off a 1999 GameFAQs thread and never thought about again. Mine isn't that.

Top 10 N64 Games🕹️⬇️
lists.outro:
Ten games. 

No Mario, no Zelda, Goldeneye sitting at five.

The N64 library was always deeper than the list everyone keeps copying off each other. Most people just never looked past it.
lists.heading: Top 10 N64 games

items.name: Wave Race 64
items.reason: The best game on the N64 doesn't have a single enemy in it.
items.more:
In 1996 nobody had seen water move like this on a home console. The first time you raced, the waves shoved your ski around so convincingly it almost felt broken. 

Nothing on the PS1 came close. Nothing else on the N64 did either.

No spectacle, no gimmick. Just the hardware doing something genuinely new.

items.name: Perfect Dark
items.reason: Smarter enemies than Goldeneye, more weapons, a bigger campaign, and bots so you didn't need three friends on the couch.
items.more: It came out two years later and quietly beat Goldeneye at the exact thing Goldeneye is worshipped for. Only one game on this list beats it.

items.name: Star Wars Episode I: Racer
items.reason: Better than the movie. And I'll say the thing nobody wants to: it's the best Star Wars game ever made.
items.more:
The speed felt genuinely dangerous, the tracks were trying to kill you, and I'd sink entire afternoons into upgrading a pod racer for a podrace that lasted four minutes.

People fight me on this constantly.

items.name: 1080° Snowboarding
items.reason: People don't take snowboarding games seriously so this one just gets skipped entirely.
items.more:
The physics were real, the courses actually demanded something from you, and it looked incredible for the time. 

I put more hours into this than I'd ever admit publicly.

items.name: Goldeneye 007
items.reason: Okay. Number 5.
items.more:
Yeah it mattered. It made the console shooter a real thing and a movie tie-in had no right being that good. I'm not arguing any of that.

But mattering and being the best game on the system are two different things, and four games here clear it.

items.name: Pilotwings 64
items.reason: Launched alongside the console and everyone forgot it existed by Christmas.
items.more:
No enemies, nothing to shoot, just Nintendo figuring out how to move through 3D space before anyone else had even solved the camera. 

I'll say it: as a launch game it holds up better than Mario 64, and that one always gets people.

items.name: Killer Instinct Gold
items.reason: Everyone remembers Killer Instinct on SNES. Almost nobody remembers Gold even existed.
items.more:
It was the arcade sequel, KI2, brought home nearly intact, and the N64 pulled it off better than a cartridge had any right to. Full announcer, the combo system intact, none of it watered down.

It's the best fighting game on the console and it isn't close.

items.name: San Francisco Rush: Extreme Racing
items.reason: Arcade racing on this console basically starts and ends with Rush.
items.more:
The tracks were ridiculous, there were shortcuts hidden in spots you'd only find by accident, and the crashes were the entire point. 

Every modern racing game took that out and decided it was an improvement. It wasn't.

items.name: Duke Nukem: Zero Hour
items.reason: Third person, time travel, and weirdly funny in a way the PC games never were.
items.more: Came out in 1999, sold to about nine people, and disappeared. I think it's better than half the shooters that get brought up in these threads.

items.name: Turok: Rage Wars
items.reason: Everyone acts like Goldeneye was the only multiplayer game on the N64. It wasn't.
items.more:
Turok: Rage Wars was four player and honestly meaner and faster than anything Rare did, it just had the worst possible timing, dropping right when Goldeneye was still the only thing anyone wanted to play at a sleepover.

Nobody gave it a chance.

lists.intro:
Nintendo Direct day.

No better time to finish my N64 ranking.

The top 10 is locked. Here's 20 through 11.

And this is where it gets uncomfortable, because some of the most worshipped carts Nintendo ever shipped never cracked my top 10.

Ocarina is in here. So is Mario Kart.

Reputation didn't get a vote. Time played did.
lists.outro:
That's 20 through 11. 

Here's the logic, since it always comes up.

I don't rank by review scores. I don't rank by what's "important." I rank by the carts I kept coming back to.

Hours in the controller. Not headlines.

That's why Extreme-G beats Mario Kart. That's why Ocarina is good and not gospel. That's why a wrestling game outranks Donkey Kong 64 and Rogue Squadron.

Reputation is borrowed. Time played is earned.
lists.heading: N64 games, 20 through 11

items.name: Super Mario 64
items.reason: The game that taught every 3D title how to move.
items.more:
I will never argue its importance.

But importance and fun aren't the same thing, and I reach for a dozen other carts before this one.

Historic. Not my number one.

items.name: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
items.reason: Here it is.
items.more:
A good game. A genuinely good game.

Not the greatest of all time. Not even my favorite on the console.

Zelda is the most overrated name in gaming, and this is exhibit A.

Good. Just not untouchable.

items.name: Star Fox 64
items.reason: Do a barrel roll.
items.more:
The rumble pak debuted here. So did voice acting I can still quote cold.

Tight, replayable, branching paths that begged a second run.

On rails and better for it.

items.name: Diddy Kong Racing
items.reason: The kart game with a campaign.
items.more:
Planes, hovercrafts, a real adventure mode, and a boss named Wizpig living rent free in my head.

Rare at full strength.

The single player Mario Kart never bothered to build.

items.name: WWF No Mercy
items.reason: The ceiling.
items.more:
Every lesson the AKI engine learned, perfected. A create a wrestler so deep it became its own hobby.

Twenty five years later people still mod this cart.

Best wrestling game ever made. Not up for debate.

items.name: Star Wars: Rogue Squadron
items.reason: Rumble pak in hand, X-wing on screen.
items.more:
Death Star runs and Hoth fantasies finally playable in your living room.

Rough around the edges today. Pure adrenaline then.

The Star Wars game the N64 deserved.

items.name: Extreme-G
items.reason: Anti-grav racing at speeds the N64 had no business hitting.
items.more:
Weapons, tunnels, a sense of velocity that melted the framerate and my eyes right along with it.

I put more hours into this than Mario Kart. By a lot.

Better game. I said what I said.

items.name: Mario Kart 64
items.reason: I know.
items.more:
Four player split screen built a generation of friendships, and Block Fort battle mode is untouchable.

But the single player bored me, and the blue shell aged like milk.

Loved by everyone. Ranked here by me.

items.name: WWF WrestleMania 2000
items.reason: The night the AKI engine finally crossed over to the WWF.
items.more:
WCW hoarded that magic for two years. World Tour. Revenge.

Then the grappling system, the create modes, and a career that actually mattered all landed in a WWF cart.

The blueprint. Not the masterpiece.

items.name: Donkey Kong 64
items.reason: The expansion pak game.
items.more:
Five characters, a hundred kinds of collectible, and a coconut launcher.

Ambitious to a fault.

I respect the scope more than I enjoyed the grind.

lists.intro:
Most people rank PS1 games based on pure, unearned nostalgia, pristine jewel case counts, or 30 year old review scores from magazines that don't hold up today. 

They build these safe, predictable top 10 lists that look exactly the same because they are afraid to challenge the established consensus. 

This list is going to completely break the brains of traditional purists who think critical acclaim equals elite design, but it is the only accurate evaluation of what actually made this hardware legendary.

Top 10 PS1 Games🧵⬇️
lists.outro:
The golden era of the 90s belonged to developers who understood mechanical friction. 

These ten titles aren't just great games, they are the definitive, undisputed peak of the PlayStation. 

A console's legacy is built on the titles that kept a controller feeling alive in your hands, and nothing else on the hardware touches this list.
lists.heading: Top 10 PS1 games

items.name: Metal Gear Solid
items.reason: The undisputed peak of the generation.
items.more:
It didn't just introduce cinematic stealth, it weaponized the physical limitations of the hardware to build tension. 

The linear pacing, unmatched voice acting, and tactile friction remain completely flawless.

items.name: Tekken 3
items.reason: The absolute pinnacle of 3D fighting.
items.more:
It forced the hardware to deliver fluid, 60 frames-per-second mechanical perfection at a time when most developers were still struggling to render basic, jagged polygons. 

It is pure combat refinement.

items.name: Mega Man Legends
items.reason: The ultimate test of design over convention, earning its spot on the podium.
items.more: It successfully transitioned a 2D icon into a fully realized 3D world with tight action and linear exploration, completely outpacing the passive, slow design of its contemporaries.

items.name: Parasite Eve
items.reason: Square's actual masterpiece on the system.
items.more: A tightly paced, 10 hour cinematic experience that respects your time and delivers vastly more storytelling impact in a single weekend than massive, sprawling, bloated 80-hour games can manage across multiple discs.

items.name: Twisted Metal 2
items.reason: The absolute peak of vehicular combat, breaking into the top five on pure mechanical execution.
items.more:
It perfectly captures the raw, unfiltered arcade energy of the mid-90s. 

The brilliant level design and tight physical controls made it a multiplayer essential that has never been duplicated.

items.name: Gran Turismo
items.reason: The definitive racing simulator that changed the entire industry.
items.more: Its technical precision, vehicle weight physics, and massive car roster established a benchmark that elevated the PlayStation's reputation from a mere toy to a mature, sophisticated machine.

items.name: WWF SmackDown! 2: Know Your Role
items.reason: The undisputed champion of the era's arcade style wrestling games.
items.more: Yuke's packed incredible speed, fluid animations, and a massive roster into a highly addictive gameplay loop that captured the exact unhinged energy of the late-90s boom period without any unnecessary filler.

items.name: Final Fantasy VII
items.reason: A massive cultural milestone with legendary production values, but the truth is the turn-based combat and text-heavy pacing drag it down.
items.more: It barely cracks the top eight because pure action-mechanics and physical responsiveness beat out menu-mashing every single time.

items.name: Syphon Filter
items.reason: A masterclass in tactical shooting and linear level design that completely outpaces the slower games of the era.
items.more: The reliance on gadgets, aggressive target locking, and fast-paced infiltration kept players fully locked into the physical friction of late-90s action.

items.name: Final Fantasy IX
items.reason: While visually impressive for a late-stage title releasing the same year as the PS2, it represents the absolute extreme end of slow, turn-based excess.
items.more: On a platform whose real legacy was built on speed and tight action, its glacial combat pacing barely earns it a spot on the board.

1. Metal Gear Solid
2. Syphon Filter
3. Final Fantasy VII

PS1 had a lot of bangers.

lists.intro:
Everybody has a console they defend to the death.

The Nintendo GameCube is the one I defend like it's my family. This console always gets ranked behind the PS2 and the Xbox. It's one of my personal favorites and I've had way more fun on this console than I did on the PS2, which is just a glorified DVD player.

Here's the Top 5 GameCube games.

There's no Mario and no Zelda on this list.

Super Mario Sunshine built the whole game around Mario having a water pack and thought that was a good idea. Nintendo decided Link should look like a cartoon and then made you sail for half of the game in Wind Waker.

Both of those franchises fell off hard this generation.

Here are the 5 games that carried the console.
lists.outro:
The GameCube is the most underrated console ever made. People remember the handle on the side and the purple case and not much else about what came out on it.

Meanwhile the PS2 gets treated like the best thing that ever happened and half the people who owned one were using it to watch movies.
lists.heading: Top 5 GameCube games

items.name: Metroid Prime
items.reason: Remaking Metroid into a first person shooter was a no brainer. I bought my GameCube in 2003 and this was the game that blew me away, and it still holds up better than almost anything else from that decade.
items.more:
The graphics felt ahead of its time. Seeing Samus' reflection in the visor was unreal. The overall gameplay was smooth and addictively fun to play.

This is the best game on the GameCube.

items.name: Star Fox Adventures
items.reason: This is the last game Rare made for Nintendo before Microsoft bought the studio.
items.more:
It's better than Wind Waker and Super Mario Sunshine and it's not particularly close.

I purchased this game with my GameCube in 2003 and immediately liked this Star Fox more than the N64 game.

items.name: Mario Kart: Double Dash
items.reason: The second best Mario Kart ever made, behind Super Mario Kart and ahead of Mario Kart 64.
items.more:
Two characters on one kart with their own special items was the only real change the series has ever made to its own formula.

Everything about this game worked and Nintendo walked away from it.

items.name: Metal Gear Solid: The Twin Snakes
items.reason: This is Metal Gear Solid from 1998 rebuilt in the engine Sons of Liberty ran on, and the only place you could play it was a Nintendo console.
items.more:
Everybody who hates this game hates it for the same two things. The cutscenes run long and Snake can shoot while he's moving. Neither one bothered me.

I've played both versions and this one is fantastic.

items.name: Super Smash Bros. Melee
items.reason: This is the game you put on when four people were over and everyone wanted in on the action.
items.more:
Smash has had a lot of sequels since then and none of them are better than this one. 

It sits at fifth because I've spent more time with the four games above it.

lists.intro:
Top 10 original Xbox games. 

The black box, not the 360.

No Half-Life 2. It got ported to Xbox, it didn't belong to it. That game lived on PC and everyone here already played it there.

Top🔟🧵⤵️
lists.outro:
That is the list. 

If you are looking for Morrowind or Half-Life 2, you missed the point of the original hardware. 

Pandora Tomorrow takes the stealth crown, Advent Rising deserved its sequel, and Halo 2 is the single reason we remember the console today.
lists.heading: Top 10 original Xbox games

items.name: Halo 2
items.reason: The reason you remember the original Xbox at all.
items.more:
Not the campaign, the nights. Xbox Live started here, and so did every trash talked match and every friendship that ended over a betrayal on Lockout. 

The single most important console game of its generation and it isn't close.

items.name: Splinter Cell: Pandora Tomorrow
items.reason: Above Halo: Combat Evolved.
items.more:
Patience as a weapon. 

This is the game that proved Xbox could do more than run and gun, that the most tense thing on the system was sitting in the dark waiting for a guard to turn around.

items.name: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic
items.reason: The best Star Wars story that never touched a movie screen.
items.more: A turn-based RPG on a console built for shooters had no business being this good, and the twist still hits harder than anything the films managed in the same era.

items.name: Halo: Combat Evolved
items.reason: Fourth. I said what I said.
items.more:
It proved a console shooter could work, then its own sequel did everything it did and built a community on top of it. 

History remembers it as the launch that mattered. 

It's still the fourth best game on its own console.

items.name: DOOM 3
items.reason: Made you afraid of the dark again and everyone whined about the flashlight instead of admitting they were scared.
items.more:
The people who actually finished it never forgot it. 

The people who complained never got past the first lab.

items.name: Advent Rising
items.reason: The ambitious swing nobody remembers.
items.more:
A flawed, gorgeous mess that aimed higher than games with triple its budget. 

It reached for something most games never even attempt, and it landing at six over the consensus favorites is intentional.

items.name: Project Gotham Racing 2
items.reason: The best racing game on the system and it isn't a debate. Kudos chasing was an addiction before anyone had a word for it.
items.more: Forza gets the legacy. PGR2 had the soul.

items.name: 007: NightFire
items.reason: The Bond shooter that actually delivered.
items.more:
It lifted the GoldenEye blueprint and didn't embarrass it, which is more than almost every licensed game of its era can say. 

Better than half the "serious" shooters people put on these lists.

items.name: MechAssault
items.reason: Stomping through a building never stopped being satisfying.
items.more:
One of the first games that made Xbox Live feel like the entire point of owning the console instead of a bonus feature. 

Ignored by too many back then, completely forgotten today. Criminal on both fronts.

items.name: Justice League Heroes
items.reason: Yes. This, and not the other co-op game everyone defaults to.
items.more: Four-player couch co-op with the DC roster, and it earned its spot. I stand by it.

lists.intro:
Modern developers hide behind 4K textures and endless sandbox maps to mask hollow gameplay. 

True mechanical perfection was achieved decades ago.

These are the top 10 greatest games of all time, and the industry has been chasing them ever since.

Top 10 greatest games🧵⤵️
lists.outro:
These 10 games built the foundation of the industry, and not a single modern release has done enough to knock them off this list.

They didn't rely on day one patches, season passes, or endless digital roadmaps to be great.

They delivered perfect, self-contained experiences right out of the box, and given the current state of modern gaming, their spots on this list are permanently secured.
lists.heading: Top 10 greatest games of all time

items.name: Super Mario Bros. 3
items.reason: It didn't just define platforming; it wrote the absolute rulebook.
items.more: The physics, the world map secrets, and the sheer variety of level design created a standard that modern developers are still failing to replicate.

items.name: Halo: Combat Evolved
items.reason: The encounter design in the Silent Cartographer alone is better than most entire modern campaigns.
items.more: It proved a console shooter could deliver a sweeping narrative while keeping the combat loop perfectly paced.

items.name: Mega Man Legends
items.reason: Exploring the ruins of Kattelox Island gave us a living, breathing 3D world with upgrade mechanics that felt genuinely rewarding.
items.more: It was a massive departure for the franchise that completely nailed the execution.

items.name: Contra
items.reason: Pure, distilled arcade action brought to the living room.
items.more:
It doesn't hold your hand or let you rely on a forgiving checkpoint system. 

You either memorize the enemy patterns and master the spread gun, or you get a game over.

items.name: Super Mario World
items.reason: Taking the flawless foundation of its predecessor and expanding it with branching paths and cape feather physics.
items.more: It is the absolute pinnacle of 16-bit platforming and the gold standard for launch titles.

items.name: Metal Gear Solid
items.reason: It bridged the gap between cinema and gaming without ever forgetting it was a game.
items.more: The tactical espionage action and the pacing of the Shadow Moses incident have never been matched.

items.name: Batman Returns
items.reason: The SNES version is a masterclass in how to handle a movie tie-in.
items.more: It took the core mechanics of a traditional beat-em-up, layered it with the brutal aesthetic of the film, and gave us the best brawler of the era.

items.name: Star Wars: Episode I Racer
items.reason: The sense of blistering speed and the risk-reward system of boosting until your engines caught fire made this an absolute standout.
items.more: Earning money to upgrade your pod actually required skill on the track.

items.name: Super Mario Kart
items.reason: It didn't just rely on Mode 7 graphics to impress us; it invented the entire kart racing genre.
items.more: Hitting a perfect drift on Ghost Valley or Rainbow Road still requires absolute mechanical precision today.

items.name: Sonic the Hedgehog
items.reason: Sega built a physics system entirely based on momentum and verticality.
items.more: The original hardware handled the sheer speed flawlessly, creating an experience that relies purely on reflexes instead of just level memorization.

lists.intro:
Every Zelda ranking you come across puts the same games in the same order, and Ocarina of Time is almost always sitting at the top of it.

I own seven Zelda games and here's how I rank them.

The one I put at number 1 is probably going to upset a lot of people.
lists.outro:
Nintendo took one real swing with this series and it was the second game.

Everything after it has been the same game, only prettier and bigger.

These are my personal rankings of the Zelda games I own. I will say I am looking forward to the Ocarina remake.
lists.heading: The Zelda games I own, ranked

items.name: Legend of Zelda: The Adventure of Link (NES)
items.reason: Zelda II is the only game in this series that ever took a real risk.
items.more:
Nintendo had a massive hit and then turned the whole thing sideways with side scrolling, experience points, and a difficulty curve that runs people off, and they never had the nerve to try anything like it again. 

It's better than Ocarina of Time, and most of the people who put it last quit at Death Mountain.

items.name: Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds (3DS)
items.reason: Same Hyrule as A Link to the Past, 22 years later.
items.more:
Ravio rents you the entire item list at the start, so the dungeons open in whatever order you want them. 

Best Zelda Nintendo has made since the 90s.

items.name: The Legend of Zelda (NES)
items.reason: The one that started it.
items.more:
Empty inventory, an overworld you can walk in any direction, and nine dungeons you have to find yourself. 

Nothing tells you where to go, and that's the whole game.

items.name: Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask (N64)
items.reason: Same engine, darker game, and a far more entertaining one.
items.more:
That moon coming down is straight up nightmare fuel and there's nothing else in the series that ever tried anything like it. 

This is the better Nintendo 64 Zelda and it isn't particularly close.

items.name: Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (N64)
items.reason: I rented this from Blockbuster right after it came out and kept it the whole week, and seeing Link running around a 3D world was unlike anything else on the system at the time.
items.more:
Then it got boring. 

It was fun in 1998, and it has not aged well at all.

items.name: Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild (Switch)
items.reason: This is the prettiest game on the list and one of the slowest games I've played.
items.more:
Everything takes forever, and by the time I was climbing another wall in the rain waiting for stamina to come back I stopped caring where I was going. 

Beautiful world, and I was bored inside it.

items.name: Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Seasons (Game Boy Color)
items.reason: Capcom made this one, not Nintendo.
items.more: It's a full Zelda squeezed onto a Game Boy Color cart, with a rod that swaps the world between the four seasons to open up paths. Good game, smallest one here.

lists.intro:
Star Fox 64 is not the best Star Fox game.

I was talking about it with a coworker today who swears it's the best one.

The SNES original is the best one made. I rented it from Blockbuster in the early 90s and nothing else on the Super Nintendo looked like that.

Star Fox Adventures is my favorite. Rare's last Nintendo game and people still won't forgive it for not being an on rails shooter.

Star Fox 64 is third.

items.name: Star Fox (SNES)
items.reason: The SNES original is the best one made.

lists.intro:
Batman has the strangest legacy in gaming.

For two decades his games were mostly movie tie-ins and licensed filler. Studios slapped the cowl on whatever was in theaters and shipped it.

Then Arkham Asylum landed and proved a Batman game could actually be great.

I pulled every Batman game I own off the shelf and
ranked the 10 best.

You're going to question some of these picks.

Top 10🧵⤵️
lists.outro:
That's my top ten.

I left some off, and yeah, City at one isn't a hot take.

The real argument is two 16 bit brawlers sitting in my
top three over two Arkham games.

Tell me I'm wrong. I already know half of you will.
lists.heading: Top 10 Batman games

items.name: Batman: Arkham City
items.reason: The peak.
items.more:
Open Gotham, the deepest villain roster in any Batman game, not a wasted hour in it. 

Everything Asylum proved could work, with a whole city to prove it in. 

Nothing has touched it since.

items.name: Batman: Arkham Asylum
items.reason: The one that proved a great Batman game was even
items.more:
possible. 

Tightest of the series, no filler, no open world to pad the runtime. 

The retro classics had heart. This had everything.

items.name: Batman Returns (SNES)
items.reason: Konami took a Tim Burton movie and built a brawler that stands next to Turtles in Time.
items.more:
Tight, mean, stacked with moves. 

A licensed SNES beat-em-up beating two Arkham games is exactly the hill I'm dying on.

items.name: Batman: The Video Game (NES)
items.reason: The wall jump. The soundtrack. The blue suit nobody
items.more:
asked for and nobody forgot. 

Sunsoft turned a movie tie-in into one of the best action games on the NES.

Licensed games were not supposed to be this good.

items.name: Batman: Arkham Knight
items.reason: The best Batman has ever looked, dragged into a brawl by a tank.
items.more:
Pull the Batmobile out and this is top-two Arkham. 

It lands at five because two 16-bit games did more with less. 

That's not a knock. That's the bar.

items.name: The Adventures of Batman & Robin (Genesis)
items.reason: A run-and-gun that doubles as a technical showcase.
items.more:
The soundtrack is one of the best on the system and the difficulty is flat out punishing. 

Proof the Genesis had real muscle when the right team showed up.

items.name: Batman: The Brave and the Bold (Wii)
items.reason: A WayForward co-op brawler nobody remembers and
items.more:
everybody should. 

Hand-drawn, fast, built for two on a couch. It got buried under a console nobody took seriously for this kind of game. 

Their loss.

items.name: Batman: Revenge of the Joker (Genesis)
items.reason: Sunsoft's follow-up nobody talks about.
items.more:
Bigger and flashier than the NES games, with color and scale the 8-bit hardware couldn't touch. 

It never hit the same highs, but it swung for them.

items.name: Batman: Vengeance (PS2)
items.reason: Built on the animated series, the only Batman that ever truly mattered.
items.more:
The game itself is a competent licensed brawler and nothing more. 

It rides this high on the strength of the source material alone.

items.name: Batman: Arkham Origins
items.reason: The Arkham game everyone writes off because Rocksteady didn't make it. Then they go finish it again every couple years.
items.more:
Best Joker writing in the series, stuck at the bottom of a list it could headline anywhere else.

Last place in this franchise is still a good game.

lists.intro:
Saturday morning X-Men on Fox Kids had every kid in the 90s fighting over who got to be Wolverine.

Ten best X-Men action games ever made.

Several controversial picks.

The best one isn't from the 90s. A movie tie-in made the top 3.

Top 10👇🧵
lists.outro: That's the best 10 X-Men games and nobody has made a better game since Legends II came out in 2005.
lists.heading: Top 10 X-Men action games

items.name: X-Men Legends II: Rise of Apocalypse, Xbox (2005)
items.reason: Apocalypse is a big enough threat that Magneto and the Brotherhood join the X-Men to fight him, which puts Sabretooth, Juggernaut and Scarlet Witch on the same team as Wolverine and Storm.
items.more: The roster is huge, and up to four people can play the whole thing together.

items.name: X-Men Legends, Xbox (2004)
items.reason: You take four X-Men into every mission and swap between them whenever you want, all the way from Magma's first day at the mansion to a war with Magneto and the Brotherhood.
items.more: The story and the ambiance are what did it for me.

items.name: X-Men Origins: Wolverine, Xbox 360/PS3 (2009)
items.reason: Hugh Jackman voices Logan in the Uncaged Edition, the version with all the gore left in.
items.more:
When he takes enough damage you can see down to the adamantium, then watch it all grow back.

Still a better game than Insomniac's Wolverine.

items.name: X-Men 2: Clone Wars, Sega Genesis (1995)
items.reason: Seven playable characters, and Magneto is one of them, which almost never happened in an X-Men game back then.
items.more: Every character has their own moves and their own way through the levels, all of it up against the Phalanx.

items.name: X-Men, Sega Genesis (1993)
items.reason: Wolverine, Cyclops, Gambit and Nightcrawler all play differently, and you can call in Storm, Iceman, Rogue, Archangel or Jean Grey when you need help.
items.more: It's also the game that told you to reset the computer and meant the actual reset button on your Genesis.

items.name: X-Men: Mutant Apocalypse, SNES (1994)
items.reason: Capcom made this side-scroller in 1994, and every character in it moves and attacks completely differently.
items.more: Cyclops, Wolverine, Psylocke, Beast and Gambit each get their own opening stage before the team heads into Genosha and on to Magneto.

items.name: X2: Wolverine's Revenge, GameCube (2003)
items.reason: Mark Hamill voices Wolverine and Patrick Stewart is back as Professor X, in a story that goes all the way back to Weapon X and the day Logan got his adamantium.
items.more: The stealth sections and the berserker rage give it a lot more to do than slash through rooms.

items.name: Spider-Man & X-Men: Arcade's Revenge, SNES (1992)
items.reason: Arcade traps Spider-Man, Wolverine, Cyclops, Storm and Gambit inside Murderworld, where every one of them gets their own stages built around their powers.
items.more: It's brutally hard, and the soundtrack from Tim and Geoff Follin gets talked about more than the game does.

items.name: Wolverine: Adamantium Rage, Sega Genesis (1994)
items.reason: Acclaim gave Wolverine his own game with nobody else from the team along for it, hunting for answers about his past with a healing factor that refills his health on its own.
items.more: It gets left off almost every X-Men list anyone makes.

items.name: Uncanny X-Men, NES (1989)
items.reason: This is where my love for X-Men started.
items.more: LJN put Wolverine, Storm, Cyclops, Colossus, Iceman and Nightcrawler on one cartridge, with two players able to team up at the same time.

lists.intro:
You've been lied to about superhero games.

Every list looks the same. Same obvious picks. Same safe order. Nobody wants to actually have the conversation.

So let's have it.

My top 10 superhero games. 

From my own collection. Played every single one.

You're going to disagree.

Top🔟🧵⏬
lists.outro:
Ten games. Ten picks I'll defend without hesitation.

The superhero genre has produced more misses than hits. These are the ones that got it right.

Every copy on this list is sitting on my shelf. I've played them all. This is what the genre looks like when it's done properly.

Arkham City is the ceiling. The rest of the list proves the floor was higher than most people remember.
lists.heading: Top 10 superhero games

items.name: Batman: Arkham City (2011)
items.reason: Not a debate. Not a conversation.
items.more:
Every superhero game released after 2011 gets measured against this one. Most don't survive the comparison.

The combat. The world. The writing. The villains.

One of the best video games ever made.

items.name: Marvel: Ultimate Alliance (2006)
items.reason: 20+ playable heroes. Co-op that made you call your friends.
items.more:
Nobody makes superhero games like this anymore and the genre is worse for it.

Every modern superhero game is a solo cinematic experience. Ultimate Alliance was a party.

We lost something when this era ended.

items.name: Deadpool (2013)
items.reason: Not the best superhero game ever made. Not even close.
items.more:
But it might be the most fun.

The writing is sharp. The self-awareness works. It commits completely to what it is and never apologizes for it.

A game that knew exactly what it was. Rare.

items.name: Batman Begins (2005)
items.reason: A movie tie-in has zero business being this good.
items.more:
Someone understood Batman as a predator and built accordingly. The fear mechanic was ahead of its time.

Arkham gets the credit. Begins did it first.

items.name: Marvel's Spider-Man (2018)
items.reason: Technically brilliant. Visually stunning. The swinging finally felt right.
items.more:
So why is it only 5?

Because polished isn't the same as memorable. I finished it. I respected it. I didn't fall in love with it.

That gap is the difference between 5 and 1.

items.name: Spider-Man & Venom: Maximum Carnage (1994)
items.reason: The red cartridge alone deserves a spot on the list.
items.more:
But the game backs it up. 

Relentless. Hard. Unapologetic.

Peak 16-bit superhero energy. Nobody was doing it better on that hardware.

items.name: Justice League Heroes (2006)
items.reason: Go ahead. Say it.
items.more:
I know what you're thinking. And you're not entirely wrong.

But sit down with this game and actually play it. The combat works. The roster delivers. It does exactly what it sets out to do.

Underrated. Intentionally placed here.

items.name: X-Men Legends II: Rise of Apocalypse (2005)
items.reason: The best Marvel action RPG ever made.
items.more:
Massive roster. Co-op that actually worked. A story that respected the source material.

The fact that nobody makes games like this anymore is one of gaming's great unsolved crimes.

items.name: Captain America and the Avengers (1992)
items.reason: Four playable characters. Co-op beat-em-up that held up better than most of what came after it.
items.more:
Cap felt like Cap. The roster felt earned.

The 16-bit era understood the assignment on this one.

items.name: X2: Wolverine's Revenge (2003)
items.reason: Nobody talks about this game anymore and that's a problem.
items.more:
Wolverine actually felt dangerous. The stealth mechanics worked. The story respected the character.
It got buried under better marketing for worse games.

Forgotten. Shouldn't be.

lists.intro:
Every Star Wars top 10 you have ever read starts with KOTOR at number one. Every one of them is wrong.

I own 17 Star Wars games. Cartridge and disc, NES through Switch, all of it on the shelf behind me. I didn't read about these games. I played them, beat them, and went back to the ones worth going back to.

That last part is the entire list. I ranked these by how many times I actually reloaded them, not by what a magazine scored them in 2003.

So the best reviewed Star Wars game I own finished fourth. The game most people would crown number one finished second. And the one sitting at the top came out of the movie everybody loves to hate.

Worst to first. If your number one is KOTOR, this is going to bother you.
lists.outro:
The full list, worst to first:

10. The Empire Strikes Back
9. Starfighter: Special Edition
8. Knights of the Old Republic II
7. Battlefront
6. Jedi Starfighter
5. Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy
4. Knights of the Old Republic
3. Super Star Wars
2. Rogue Squadron
1. Episode I: Racer

Every other Star Wars list ranks these by what a critic typed 20 years ago. I ranked them by how many times I actually walked to the shelf, pulled the case, and put the disc back in.

That is why a 94 sits at four and a podracer sits at one. The reputation lists are the lazy ones.
lists.heading: Top 10 Star Wars games

items.name: Star Wars Episode I: Racer (N64)
items.reason: More than 20 tracks, engines you nurse and repair between heats, and a sense of speed the N64 had no business producing. I logged more hours here than anything else on this entire list, by a wide margin.
items.more:
The pods, the announcer, the Boonta Eve circuit burned into memory. This is the rare tie-in that was flat out better than the thing it was based on.

The best Star Wars game ever made came out of the worst Star Wars movie ever made. If KOTOR is your number one, you ranked the reviews. I ranked the games.

items.name: Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (N64)
items.reason: X-wings through canyons, the Expansion Pak humming, the trench-run fantasy pulled off better than any game before it or since. This is the one that made the N64 feel like a flight sim with a soul.
items.more:
If I were ranking by reputation, this is your number one and we would both move on.

I am not ranking by reputation. It lands at two, and the one game ahead of it is going to start a fight.

items.name: Super Star Wars (SNES)
items.reason: A 16-bit run-and-gun so hard it ran grown adults off the controller. The Sarlacc, the Tusken Raiders, the Mode 7 Landspeeder stage that still looks incredible 30 years on.
items.more:
I have put more hours into this cartridge than both KOTOR games combined, and it is not particularly close.

A SNES platformer ranking above the two RPGs this fanbase worships is going to bother people. It bothers them because it is correct.

items.name: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic (Xbox)
items.reason: The highest reviewed game in my entire collection. The Revan twist is still the best single moment these games have ever produced. I am not going to insult it.
items.more:
But here is what the people crowning it number one will not say out loud. It is a phenomenal story bolted to combat that was already dated the day it launched, a dice roll dressed up as a swordfight.

I have finished KOTOR. I have zero urge to ever finish it again. The nine games around it I reload constantly. Reputation carried this to fourth. Nothing was carrying it higher.

items.name: Star Wars Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy (Xbox)
items.reason: Build your own saber. Single, dual, or staff. Pick a stance. Then cut through a room and feel every swing land.
items.more:
This is the best lightsaber combat ever put in a game, and I am including everything released since. Fallen Order and Survivor are great. Neither one topped a 2003 port.

The only thing holding it out of the top three is a campaign that never matched the swordplay. Fifth.

items.name: Star Wars: Jedi Starfighter (PS2)
items.reason: The sequel nobody mentions. They wired Force powers into your ship, gave you Nym as a wingman, and built something tighter and stranger than the original Starfighter in every single way.
items.more:
It reviewed fine, sold fine, then vanished from the conversation completely.

It is the most underrated Star Wars game I own and it is not close. The fact that it sits above Battlefront should tell you how serious I am.

items.name: Star Wars: Battlefront (Xbox)
items.reason: The 2004 original. Split screen, a buddy on the couch, Hoth turning the living room into a warzone for a weekend.
items.more:
Now the honest part. Half of you defending this in the replies never actually played the 2004 version. You are remembering Battlefront II from 2005 and calling it nostalgia.

Stripped of the sequel's reputation, the original is shallow and repeats itself fast. Seventh, and lucky to be on the list at all.

items.name: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II (Xbox)
items.reason: Obsidian took the first game and pointed it somewhere darker and smarter. Kreia is the best written character in either KOTOR, full stop, and the game has more interesting things to say about the Force than the entire prequel trilogy.
items.more:
Then it shipped with the back half gutted. You need a fan mod just to see the ending the writers actually wrote.

The crowd calling this the better KOTOR is grading an unfinished game on a curve. Brilliant and broken still loses to merely great.

items.name: Star Wars Starfighter: Special Edition (Xbox)
items.reason: Launch-window Xbox, built to prove the hardware could fly. Squadrons over Naboo, capital ships filling the screen, the exact kind of thing that sold the console off a Circuit City demo kiosk.
items.more:
Here is the problem. I remember precisely how it looked and almost nothing about how it played.

A game I recall as a screensaver does not climb any higher. Ninth, and ninth is generous.

items.name: Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (NES)
items.reason: This is the one where you took down AT-ATs with a tow cable, on a console that punished you for blinking. The Dagobah swamp alone ended more rentals than it ever finished.
items.more:
It is rough. It is unfair in the exact way only late-80s licensed games knew how to be.

And it still made the list over Demolition, Lightsaber Duels, and half a dozen others I own. The bottom of this list clears a higher bar than the top of most people's.

lists.intro:
007 First Light has released. 

It has 30+ years of history to live up to. 

My top 5 Bond games of all time. 🧵⬇️
lists.outro:
Five games. Thirty years of Bond on console. One bar that's never been cleared.

007 First Light is out. I want to be wrong, but I'm not confident it holds up.

Modern studios forgot how to make shooters fun 15 years ago.
lists.heading: Top 5 James Bond games

items.name: GoldenEye 007
items.reason: Not up for debate.
items.more:
Changed what console shooters could be, defined a generation of multiplayer, and still one of the biggest games in pop culture history.

Nothing in the franchise has touched it in 30 years.

items.name: Everything or Nothing
items.reason: The most ambitious Bond game ever made before today.
items.more:
Third person, original story, Hollywood cast, Pierce Brosnan, Judi Dench, Willem Dafoe, and it delivered. 

Felt like playing an actual Bond film.

Still the gold standard for what a licensed Bond game should be.

items.name: NightFire
items.reason: The one that came closest to capturing what made GoldenEye work.
items.more:
Full campaign, great multiplayer, missions that actually felt like Bond, not just a generic action game with a license slapped on it.

People forget how good this one was.

items.name: Tomorrow Never Dies
items.reason: Nobody puts this one on their list. I do.
items.more:
The PS1 era Bond game everyone forgot about. 

Solid third person shooter, legitimately fun, and it holds up better than people give it credit for.

items.name: From Russia With Love
items.reason: Based on one of the best Bond films ever made, and it shows.
items.more:
Connery's voice, classic spy tradecraft, and a mission structure that actually felt like a Bond movie instead of a shooter with a Bond skin on it.

Underrated entry that most people slept on.

lists.intro:
Ten best fighting games ever made.

No Mortal Kombat 3. No Smash Bros. Several surprise picks. 

Top 10🧵⤵️
lists.outro:
That is the ten. Virtua Fighter 2 at the bottom, Street Fighter II Turbo at the top.

Not one game from the last twenty five years made it.

The genre peaked in the 90s and nothing since has gotten close.
lists.heading: Top 10 fighting games

items.name: Street Fighter II Turbo, SNES (1993)
items.reason: Every fighting game that came after it is working off what this one figured out.
items.more:
Turbo is where it finally had everything, the four bosses playable, mirror matches, and the speed setting cranked until it became a different game. 

I rented Street Fighter II from Blockbuster so many times it would have been cheaper for my mom to just buy it. 

I still know Ryu's inputs without thinking about it.

items.name: Mortal Kombat II, Sega Genesis (1994)
items.reason: Everything the first one was missing.
items.more:
Bigger roster, better fatalities, Kitana and Mileena and Scorpion and Sub-Zero all in their prime, and secret characters half the kids at school swore they had found. 

This is the peak of the entire franchise and nothing since has come close.

items.name: Tekken 3, PlayStation (1998)
items.reason: There is not a bad character on the roster.
items.more:
Jin, Hwoarang, Eddy, Yoshimitsu, King, and a bear. 

Namco fit the entire arcade game onto a PlayStation disc with almost nothing lost and threw in Tekken Force and Tekken Ball on top. 

Best 3D fighter ever made.

items.name: TMNT: Tournament Fighters, SNES (1993)
items.reason: Konami made a genuinely great fighting game and put the Turtles in it.
items.more:
Super meter, story mode, sprites straight off the arcade screen, and a roster deep enough to have Karai and Wingnut in it. 

Best licensed fighting game ever made.

items.name: Street Fighter III: Double Impact, Dreamcast (2000)
items.reason: The best looking 2D fighting game ever made and nobody can tell me otherwise.
items.more:
Hand drawn animation that still holds up 25 years later, a brand new roster with Alex, Dudley, and Ibuki, and parrying, where perfect timing lets you block a super and take nothing at all. 

Capcom rebuilt the genre from the ground up.

items.name: X-Men: Children of the Atom, Sega Saturn (1995)
items.reason: Capcom took the X-Men and gave them supers big enough to fill the whole screen.
items.more:
You could play as a Sentinel. 

Every sprite looks hand drawn off a comic page and the whole thing plays like an issue you can control.

items.name: Killer Instinct Gold, Nintendo 64 (1996)
items.reason: Everything the arcade version promised, sitting on a cartridge in your living room.
items.more:
Faster, sharper, and the combos finally land the way they were meant to with the N64 buttons under your thumbs. 

Fulgore, Glacius, Spinal, and the best announcer in the genre.

items.name: Marvel Super Heroes vs. Street Fighter, PlayStation (1999)
items.reason: Capcom threw the rulebook out for this one.
items.more:
You pick two fighters, tag them in and out, and launch somebody into the air and keep hitting them the whole way down. 

Spider-Man, Wolverine, Ryu, Chun-Li, all on one screen. 

Loudest, fastest, most ridiculous fun you can have with a fighting game.

items.name: Killer Instinct, SNES (1995)
items.reason: Nothing else on the SNES looked or sounded like this.
items.more:
The pre-rendered fighters, the announcer screaming the combo count at you, C-C-C-COMBO BREAKER, and a soundtrack people still buy on vinyl. 

Rare put an arcade game on a cartridge and the whole school lost their minds over it.

items.name: Virtua Fighter 2, Sega Saturn (1995)
items.reason: Sega had 3D fighting figured out before anybody else did.
items.more:
No fireballs and no supers, just two fighters and everything riding on your spacing and your timing. Akira, Wolf, and Jacky ran the arcade for a solid year. 

It looked unreal in 1995 and it still moves beautifully today.

lists.intro:
The best beat 'em up ever made is not the one you are about to name.

Not Streets of Rage 2. Not Final Fight. It is a licensed game and a home port, and it still beats everything the genre ever produced.

Ten best, all on my shelf. 

Counting down to a number one that is going to start an argument.

Top 10🧵⤵️
lists.outro:
The original Double Dragon started this whole genre and did not make my top ten. Streets of Rage 2 is a genre titan and it did not take the top spot. 

That is how stacked this list is.

Every game here is off my own shelf, and the number one is the one nobody expects.
lists.heading: Top 10 beat 'em ups

items.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles IV: Turtles in Time
items.reason: The best beat 'em up ever made.
items.more:
Throwing a Foot Soldier straight into the screen is the single most perfect moment the genre ever produced, and no game before or since has topped it. 

A licensed game and a home port, sitting at the top of the whole genre.

items.name: Streets of Rage 2
items.reason: The best beat 'em up Sega ever made.
items.more:
Axel, Blaze, Max, Koshiro at the peak of his powers, a difficulty curve that never once cheats you. On almost any list this is number one. 

It had the misfortune of sharing a genre with the game above it.

items.name: Final Fight
items.reason: Number three, and it belongs there.
items.more:
Haggar suplexing a Mad Gear thug carries more weight than most of the genre. 

I own the gutted SNES port with one player and no Guy, and it still lands this high.

items.name: Batman Returns
items.reason: The game most of you forgot was a brawler at all.
items.more:
Konami built a genuinely mean beat 'em up out of a movie license, and putting two thugs through a plate glass window still feels better than it should. 

Fourth is not a courtesy slot.

items.name: Spiderman Venom: Maximum Carnage
items.reason: Sixteen straight levels of getting swarmed, and it never once lets up.
items.more:
You switch between Spiderman and Venom, the difficulty is genuinely mean, and it moves faster and hits harder than any comic book brawler had a right to. 

Most licensed games from this era were forgettable. 

This one is the exception.

items.name: Streets of Rage
items.reason: This is where Sega planted the flag.
items.more: Koshiro's soundtrack in 1991 sounded like it came from a decade later, and every brawler that followed borrowed from what this game built.

items.name: River City Ransom
items.reason: It put an RPG inside a brawler before anyone knew they wanted one.
items.more:
You buy your moves, you eat to get stronger, and every enemy yells BARF when he drops. 

Nothing else on the NES moved like it.

items.name: Double Dragon II
items.reason: This is where the series finally understood itself.
items.more:
The Cyclone Kick, the brutal back half, and a co-op mode that turns on you the second you get sloppy. 

It buries the original, which did not make this list at all.

items.name: Golden Axe II
items.reason: The better Golden Axe, and I will not pretend otherwise.
items.more:
Cleaner combat, tighter levels, and I still kick the little thieves to steal their potions every time. 

The first game gets the credit and this one earns it.

items.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Hyperstone Heist
items.reason: This is what Genesis owners got instead of Turtles in Time, and Konami did not mail it in.
items.more: It is shorter and meaner than people remember, and I would still rather replay it than most of what came after.

lists.intro:
👑 Your Favorite Arcade Game is NOT in My Top 5. The FINAL 80s/90s List.

You won't agree with the ranking, but I'll stand by the logic for every single game on this list. Ready to start the argument?

A Thread🧵⤵️
lists.heading: Top 10 80s and 90s arcade games

items.name: TMNT: Turtles in Time (1991)
items.reason: The GOAT. If you rank this game lower than #1, you were a solo player with no friends.

items.name: The Simpsons Arcade Game (1991)
items.reason: The absolute peak of licensed, four-player chaos. Worth every single quarter.

items.name: Street Fighter II (1991)
items.reason: The game that invented the combo system and defined the character design, music, and art style for every fighting game that followed.

items.name: Mortal Kombat 2 (1993)
items.reason: The digitized gorefest that directly sparked the U.S. Congressional hearings which led to the creation of the ESRB.

items.name: NBA Jam (1993)
items.reason: The most iconic basketball video game ever made. This is where you got *BOOM SHAKALAKA* from.

items.name: NFL Blitz (1997)
items.reason: The only football game that explicitly included a late-hit button purely to encourage and reward spectacular post-whistle wrestling moves.

items.name: Pac-Man (1980)
items.reason: The most famous machine ever built, yet its gameplay is utterly simple.

items.name: Daytona USA (1994)
items.reason: The 3D racing masterpiece that showed off Sega’s Model 2 board, living on thanks to its infectious, sing-along soundtrack ("Let's Go Away") and force-feedback steering.

items.name: Area 51 (1995)
items.reason: The dual-gun shooter that capitalized on the 90s conspiracy craze, selling over 20,000 units and hiding the Kronn Hunter Mode for dedicated players.

items.name: Star Wars Trilogy Arcade (1998)
items.reason: Pure fan service with motion-controlled lightsaber duels. It was the peak of late 90s arcade spectacle and immersive experience.

lists.intro:
My top 10 trilogies in gaming.

Metal Gear Solid is not in the top three.

Ten series that got it right three times in a row, which is more than most franchises manage once.

Top 10🧵⬇️
lists.outro:
That's my top 10 greatest video game trilogies of all time.

No Gears of War. No Killzone. No Crash. No Uncharted.

Three great games in a row is harder than one masterpiece, and most of the biggest names have never pulled it off.
lists.heading: Top 10 video game trilogies

items.name: Super Mario Bros. 1-3
items.reason: The controls still feel right forty years later.
items.more:
Pick one up cold and you know what to do in about four seconds.

Everything else on this list I'd have to explain to somebody first. Not these three.

items.name: Halo CE / 2 / 3
items.reason: Four controllers, one TV, somebody's basement.
items.more:
Then Halo 2 put those same four people online and Halo 3 is where everybody finished it.

Six years of your life ran alongside these three games. That's why people won't let go of them.

items.name: Batman Arkham Asylum / City / Knight
items.reason: The Scarecrow section fakes a system crash. The screen glitches and the intro replays with Joker in Batman's place. People thought their disc was ruined.
items.more:
Freeflow combat started here and every superhero game since has copied it.

Knight included, no matter what people decided about the Batmobile in 2015.

items.name: Sonic 1-3
items.reason: Sonic 1 is the reason people walked out of the store with a Genesis instead of a SNES.
items.more:
Sonic 2 added the spin dash and Tails. Sonic 3 put a save battery in a platformer cart.

Sonic 3 is the best of the three and the series has never gotten close since.

items.name: Metal Gear Solid 1-3
items.reason: Psycho Mantis reads your memory card and tells you what else you've been playing. You beat him by moving the controller to port two.
items.more:
MGS3 drops you in a jungle with a knife and lets you starve.  

Best three-game run of the PlayStation era, and it's fifth.

items.name: Syphon Filter 1-3
items.reason: The taser. Hold the button and the guy screams, smokes, then catches fire. The camera swings around behind him so you have to watch.
items.more:
Everyone who played this remembers doing it on purpose.

Three games in three years. Then Sony sat on it for two decades and spent that money on Concord instead.

items.name: Mortal Kombat 1-3
items.reason: Midway digitized real actors while everyone else drew sprites, then put fatalities on top and got Congress involved.
items.more:
The ESRB exists because of this.  

MK3 is the weakest of the three and the one everybody names as their favorite.

items.name: Gran Turismo 1-3
items.reason: It made you pass a license test before it would let you race. Nobody would ship that today.
items.more: Every sim racer since is running off GT3 and pretending otherwise.

items.name: Desert Strike / Jungle Strike / Urban Strike
items.reason: Three games in four years.
items.more:
Isometric helicopter combat with fuel gauges and hostages and no map holding your hand.  

EA has never made anything with this much personality since.

items.name: Extreme-G / Extreme-G 2 / XGIII
items.reason: Acclaim got an N64 running at 300mph. The screen turned to streaks and the framerate held.
items.more:
Then they put weapons on the bikes.  

Two on the N64, one on the GameCube, and it got faster every time.

lists.intro:
Here's my top 5 video game trilogies. 

1. Halo 1-3
2. Batman Arkham Series
3. Super Mario 1-3
4. Sonic 1-3
5. Gears of War 1-3

Bonus: Donkey Kong Country, Metal Gear Solid, Dead Space
