lists.intro:
Today Sega turns 66.

The company that lost the console war and somehow made better games while losing it.

The 10 best Sega games ever made. Console doesn't matter. Every one of these sits on my shelf.

Ranked, definitive, no apologies. 

You'll make it three deep before you want to fight me.
lists.outro:
That's the 10.

Sixty-six years of a company that played it loud and fast and built a catalog half this industry is still borrowing from.

Every game on this list still earns its spot on my shelf, and most of them still earn a play. That is the only test that counts.

Happy birthday, Sega!
lists.heading: Top 10 Sega games

items.name: Sonic the Hedgehog 2
items.reason: The best game Sega ever made. Not Sonic 3. Not Sonic & Knuckles. The second one.
items.more:
Chemical Plant Zone. The spin dash. Speed that actually felt like speed in 1992.

This is the game that made Nintendo sweat. Everything Sega built after was chasing this high.

items.name: Shenmue
items.reason: A game about finding sailors and working forklift shifts, and it quietly rewrote the rulebook.
items.more:
Open worlds, QTEs, day/night cycles, NPCs with real schedules. Shenmue invented half of what your favorite modern games take credit for.

Sega bet the company on it. They were right, and it still cost them everything.

items.name: Virtua Fighter 2
items.reason: The fighting game the purists pretend they remember while they replay Street Fighter.
items.more:
No fireballs. No gimmicks. Just spacing, frames, and footsies before anyone had the words for it.

The Saturn's entire reason to exist.

items.name: NFL 2K
items.reason: Put a sports game in your top 5 of anything and watch people lose it. Doing it anyway.
items.more:
NFL 2K played better than Madden in 1999, and the gap only widened from there. Sega built the best football engine of its era, and then EA bought an exclusive NFL license and wiped the whole series off the board.

We never got it back.

items.name: Crazy Taxi
items.reason: A perfect arcade game. Not a good one. Perfect.
items.more:
Grab fares, beat the clock, learn the city, chase a score that never ends. Not an ounce of fat on it.

Nobody has improved the formula in 25 years because there was nothing left to improve.

items.name: Sonic the Hedgehog 3
items.reason: Yes. Below Sonic 2. I meant it.
items.more:
Bigger, prettier, more ideas, the save system, the Knuckles setup. All of it real.

But it traded the tightness of 2 for ambition, and tightness is the thing that made Sonic, Sonic. 

Still a top 10 Sega game without breaking a sweat.

items.name: Sega Rally 2
items.reason: The best arcade racer most people never touched.
items.more:
Surface physics that actually meant something. 

Gravel, tarmac, snow, each one handled different back when "realistic driving" was still a marketing lie everywhere else.

Daytona gets the glory. This one earned it.

items.name: Sonic Frontiers
items.reason: Here is where I lose some of you.
items.more:
Fifteen years of people swearing Sonic could not work in 3D, and then Frontiers just did it. Open zones, real momentum, combat that finally felt designed instead of bolted on.

It is not the safe pick. It is my pick. The first 3D Sonic that earned the speed.

items.name: Christmas NiGHTS into Dreams
items.reason: A free holiday demo better than most full games Sega shipped afterward.
items.more:
Flying, looping, scoring, dreaming. NiGHTS understood flow as a design idea before the industry had a name for it.

The fact that I'm ranking the Christmas version tells you everything about how good that engine was.

items.name: Sonic the Hedgehog
items.reason: Where all of it started. The pack-in that turned a struggling hardware company into Nintendo's only real threat.
items.more:
Green Hill Zone is still the most recognizable level in the medium. The loops, the speed, the attitude, the entire personality of 90s Sega lives in this one cartridge.

It lands at 10 because the sequel did everything here better. That is not an insult. That is a dynasty.

lists.intro:
47 years of Capcom today.

My top 10 Capcom games.

No Resident Evil. No Devil May Cry. No Monster Hunter.

I already know exactly how this thread is going to go.

Top 10🧵⤵️
lists.outro:
Ten Capcom games. 

A pizza mascot at the bottom, a Mega Man spin-off over Street Fighter II at the top.

That is my list, and I am not moving a single one.
lists.heading: Top 10 Capcom games

items.name: Mega Man Legends (PS1)
items.reason: A fully 3D action adventure in 1997 that still controls better than games released three console generations later.
items.more:
Kattelox Island, the lock on shooting, Roll and the Caskets, a world with more charm than entire studios manage today. 

Capcom built something genuinely special here and then walked away from it for good.

Putting it above Street Fighter II is the most correct thing I will post all year.

items.name: Street Fighter II (SNES)
items.reason: The most important fighting game ever made. Full stop.
items.more:
It turned the SNES into a must own machine, conjured the entire competitive fighting scene out of thin air, and set the template every fighter still follows three decades later.

And it is still only number two on this list.

items.name: Mega Man Legends 2 (PS1)
items.reason: A sequel that went bigger in every direction and got buried for the effort.
items.more:
More world, deeper systems, and an ending that stranded the hero on the moon waiting for a sequel Capcom killed in 2011.

One of the great abandoned franchises in this company's history, and the second best thing they ever pressed onto a disc.

items.name: Onimusha: Warlords (PS2)
items.reason: Resident Evil with a katana, dropped into feudal Japan.
items.more:
Fixed cameras, deliberate combat, soul absorption through the Oni Gauntlet, and a Sengoku setting nobody else had the nerve to touch. 

It became Capcom's first million seller on the PS2 for a reason.

People forgot it existed within a single generation, and that is a crime.

items.name: Disney's Chip 'n Dale: Rescue Rangers (NES)
items.reason: Drop the cartoon nostalgia for a second and just look at the design.
items.more:
Pick up a box, throw it, stack it, real two player co op that actually worked on the NES. Tight controls, smart level layouts, zero filler.

Capcom's Disney run on the NES is the most underrated stretch in their entire catalog, and this one is better built than half the fighters on this list.

items.name: X-Men: Mutant Apocalypse (SNES)
items.reason: Capcom got the X-Men license in 1994 and built a side scrolling brawler that actually took it seriously.
items.more:
You pick from five X-Men, each with their own moves and a charged mutant power, and you cut through Genosha against the Sentinels and Magneto.

This is the game that proved Capcom understood Marvel years before the crossover fighters ever showed up.

The peak of the cartridge era for this series.

items.name: Super Street Fighter II (SNES)
items.reason: The New Challengers, and the first time the roster ever grew.
items.more:
Cammy, Fei Long, Dee Jay and T. Hawk walked in and instantly became mains for a whole generation of kids on the carpet.

This was the definitive home version of the most important fighting roster ever assembled, and the cartridge era never topped it.

items.name: Marvel Super Heroes vs Street Fighter (PS1)
items.reason: Capcom's roster against Marvel's, two on two, with a giant Apocalypse as the final boss.
items.more:
It was loud, it was fast, and it was the first time you could put Wolverine and Ryu on the same screen at home.

Every fighting game crossover people love today started right here.

items.name: Street Fighter EX3 (PS2)
items.reason: The Street Fighter that went 3D before anyone was ready for it. It launched alongside the PS2 in 2000 and most fans wrote it off for ditching the classic look.
items.more:
It also let you fight tag team matches, something the main series would not seriously touch for years.

The black sheep of the family, and I will still defend it.

items.name: Yo! Noid (NES)
items.reason: Yes, the Domino's Pizza mascot got his own Capcom platformer in 1990, and yes, it rules.
items.more:
You yo-yo your way across New York, and every boss fight ends in a pizza eating showdown that is somehow more tense than it has any right to be.

Sharp controls, a brilliant hook, and the kind of weird that only the NES era could produce. This is the exact deep cut a real collection should be proud of.

lists.intro:
Acclaim caused a Senate hearing, put a word in the dictionary, and shipped a cartridge people still remember by its color.

Ten Acclaim-published games ranked by cultural impact.

Number 1 is the reason every game you own has a rating on the box.

Top 10🧵⤵️
lists.outro:
One publisher. 

A Senate hearing, a word that outlived the console it came from, a comic property saved by its own adaptation, and a logo that turned into an insult.

Acclaim did more to the culture in fifteen years than most publishers manage in forty.
lists.heading: Top 10 Acclaim games by cultural impact

items.name: Mortal Kombat (SNES / Genesis)
items.reason: Acclaim is the reason the ESRB exists.
items.more:
December 1993, Lieberman and Kohl hold Senate hearings. 

Not because of an arcade cabinet. Because this game was now in living rooms, and Acclaim is the company that put it there. Nintendo pulled the blood. Sega left it in behind a code. 

Genesis outsold SNES on this game and the entire industry read the receipt.

Every rating on every box you have ever bought traces back to a home port Acclaim published.

No other company on this list caused federal legislation. 

Not Konami. Not Capcom. Not Nintendo.

items.name: NBA Jam (SNES)
items.reason: "Boomshakalaka" left the video game and entered the English language.
items.more:
That is the rarest thing on this list by a mile. People who have never held a controller say "he's on fire." 

Broadcasters say it on live TV. It escaped the medium completely.

Midway built it. Acclaim put it in ten million houses.

items.name: Spider-Man & Venom: Maximum Carnage (SNES)
items.reason: A red cartridge. That is the whole pitch and it worked.
items.more:
1994 comics were a marketing machine running at full tilt. Fourteen part crossover, chromium covers, Venom on every rack, and Acclaim shipped it in a cart color nobody else was using.

Thirty years later people who never finished it still remember holding it. 

Ask a guy who sold his collection in 2003 what color Maximum Carnage was. He knows.

items.name: Turok 2: Seeds of Evil (N64)
items.reason: Acclaim took a dead Valiant comic property nobody was asking about and turned Turok into a household name.
items.more:
That almost never happens. Licenses run one direction, comic to game, and the game is always the lesser thing. 

Acclaim reversed it. Ask anyone under 45 what Turok is and they say N64. They do not say comics. The adaptation ate the original.

And Iguana was in-house, so this one is theirs top to bottom.

items.name: WWF WrestleMania (NES)
items.reason: Hulkamania at its absolute peak, Saturday mornings, Slim Jims, the action figures, the whole machine running at full speed.
items.more:
Acclaim held the license during the biggest mainstream wrestling window this country has ever had. 

The game is six wrestlers and a health bar. Nobody cared. You were Hogan in your living room and that was the entire product.

items.name: The Simpsons: Bart vs. the Space Mutants (NES)
items.reason: The first Simpsons game, dropped at the exact peak of Simpsons mania.
items.more:
Butterfinger ads, "Do the Bartman" on the radio, Bart shirts getting banned from schools.

The game is rough and it does not matter even slightly. 

This cart sold on a haircut. That is cultural gravity you cannot design, you can only be standing in the right place when it hits.

items.name: Terminator 2: Judgment Day (NES)
items.reason: The best and biggest movie of not only 1991, but of all time, and Acclaim carpet bombed it. NES, Game Boy, SNES, arcade, all of it.
items.more:
This is the licensing model that defined the era and Acclaim ran it harder than anyone alive. Buy the license, ship on every platform that exists, put the poster on the box, move a million units before a single review lands.

Everybody complains about that model now. Everybody bought it then.

items.name: Double Dragon II: The Revenge (NES)
items.reason: Before Streets of Rage, before Turtles in Time, this is what a beat em up meant in a living room.
items.more:
Two players, one couch, one guy elbowing the other guy off a ledge on purpose. The entire genre's living room grammar starts here. 

Technos built it. Acclaim put it in the house.

items.name: Beetlejuice (NES)
items.reason: Influence is not always positive.
items.more:
Acclaim bought LJN in 1990 and kept putting that rainbow on licensed games for five more years. 

Beetlejuice was one of the first ones out the door under Acclaim, and it played like every joke people make about the logo.

Thirty five years later the rainbow is still an insult. That is influence.

items.name: NARC (NES)
items.reason: The D.A.R.E. era pressed into a cartridge.
items.more:
1988, Nancy Reagan on every TV, "Just Say No" on every classroom wall, and Williams Electronics builds an arcade game where you play a cop who shoots drug dealers and drives over the bodies. 

Acclaim brought it into the house. Bad port of a game that was already mean. But it is a perfect fossil. 

You cannot explain 1990 to someone without explaining that a kid could rent this.

lists.intro:
The 90s were the Wild West for adaptations.

Hollywood didn't understand games. Developers didn't understand movies.

We got a few masterpieces, and a lot of disasters.

Here are the Top 5 Best (and Bottom 5 Worst) Movies based on Games & Games based on Movies. 🧵
lists.outro:
I know putting the Super Mario Bros. movie in the Top 5 is controversial. I stand by it.

It wasn't accurate, but it was fun. That sums up the 90s. Even the "bad" stuff had personality and took massive risks.

It was the best era to be a gamer.
lists.heading: Best 5 and worst 5 90s game and movie adaptations

items.name: GoldenEye 007 (N64)
items.reason: The gold standard.
items.more:
Rare didn't just adapt a Bond movie; they invented the modern console shooter.

Four-player split-screen, proximity mines, and the Facility. It was arguably better than the film itself.

items.name: Batman Returns (SNES)
items.reason: A true beat-'em-up masterpiece.
items.more:
Konami was untouchable in this era. Huge sprites, satisfying combat, and a Danny Elfman soundtrack that pushed the sound chip to the limit.

This is how you respect a license.

items.name: Mortal Kombat (1995 Movie)
items.reason: The only time Hollywood got it right in the 90s.
items.more: It wasn't winning Oscars, but it respected the source material. The fights had weight. The casting was solid. And that techno theme song is still a banger.

items.name: Aladdin (Genesis)
items.reason: Disney animators worked directly on the sprites, and it showed.
items.more: It looked like a playable cartoon. The SNES version was decent, but the Genesis version had the sword and the speed. A visual benchmark for 16-bit gaming.

items.name: Super Mario Bros. (1993 Movie)
items.reason: Hear me out.
items.more:
It had nothing to do with the game. It was a cyberpunk fever dream. Dennis Hopper was King Koopa. The Goombas were 7 feet tall.

But it was bold, dark, and unforgettable. A true cult classic that took big risks. I unironically love it.

items.name: Batman Forever (SNES/Genesis)
items.reason: Acclaim tried to use the Mortal Kombat engine for a Batman platformer.
items.more: The result? Stiff controls, digitized graphics that looked muddy, and a grappling hook that barely worked. A sluggish mess compared to Returns.

items.name: Double Dragon (1994 Movie)
items.reason: They took a gritty street brawler and turned it into a weird, post-apocalyptic comedy.
items.more: Scott Wolf and Mark Dacascos deserved better. It ignored everything that made the game cool - specifically the energy - and replaced it with bad jokes.

items.name: Street Fighter (1994 Movie)
items.reason: Raul Julia carried this entire movie on his back.

lists.intro:
Everyone has a "Top 10 Consoles" list, but most people just copy/paste sales figures from a Wikipedia entry. 

I’m ranking these based on hardware design, physical library depth, and the "finished at launch" factor. 

If you think a console needs 4K or "live service" updates to be elite, this list isn't for you.

Top 10 Consoles of all time🧵⤵️
lists.outro:
Modern consoles feel like specialized PCs that require a 50GB patch before you can even see the title screen. 

These ten machines represent an era where you bought a game, put it in the tray, and it just worked. 

If you disagree, you’re likely just looking at a spreadsheet of sales numbers instead of the hardware on the shelf.
lists.heading: Top 10 consoles of all time

items.name: Sega Dreamcast
items.reason: The Dreamcast was years ahead of its time.
items.more:
It brought pixel perfect arcade ports home when everyone else was still struggling with low-poly 3D. 

It died too soon, but for those who value innovation and pure arcade energy over sales figures, it remains the greatest console of all time.

items.name: PlayStation 2
items.reason: The Satin Silver Slim is the best-selling console for a reason.
items.more:
The library is so deep you could spend a lifetime playing it and still find hidden gems. 

It’s almost perfect, but it’s still the runner-up to the ultimate cult classic.

items.name: Xbox 360
items.reason: The 360 Slim is the greatest Western console ever built.
items.more:
It perfected the online experience before it became a bloated, microtransaction filled mess. 

The library is massive, and the controller is still the gold standard for ergonomics.

items.name: PlayStation
items.reason: Sony didn't just enter the market; they took it over.
items.more:
The move to CD-ROM changed everything for localized RPGs and cinematic action. 

If you didn't experience the transition from 2D to 3D on this hardware, you missed the most exciting time in gaming history.

items.name: Super Nintendo
items.reason: The 16-bit era was the pinnacle of 2D art.
items.more:
The SNES took everything the NES started and perfected it. 

It’s a near perfect system with a library that has zero "filler," but it lacks the sheer variety of the top four.

items.name: Xbox
items.reason: The original Xbox was a tank.
items.more:
It brought PC-level power to the living room and changed how we viewed internal storage. 

It’s the system that proved Microsoft belonged in the space, provided you had the shelf space for it.

items.name: GameCube
items.reason: The GameCube is a masterclass in industrial design.
items.more:
It didn't care about being a DVD player like its competitors; it was built to be a dedicated gaming machine. 

The mini discs are peak physical media, and the library is high density quality.

items.name: Nintendo Entertainment System
items.reason: The gray box that saved the industry. It’s the standard for pure, unfiltered gameplay.
items.more: Every modern "masterpiece" is just standing on the shoulders of the NES, but the hardware's finicky nature keeps it from ranking higher.

items.name: Sega Genesis
items.reason: The SNES had the colors, but the Genesis had the attitude and the "Blast Processing."
items.more: It brought arcade-perfect ports into the living room and proved that gaming didn't have to be "family-friendly" to be legendary.

items.name: Nintendo 64
items.reason: Nostalgia is a hell of a drug, but the library is thin once you get past the first-party titans.
items.more: It’s a revolutionary machine, but the blurry textures and the controller design keep it at the bottom of the elite tier.

best_worst.intro:
New series starting today! 

Best and worst game I own from every year, one year a day, beginning with 1985.

Best: Super Mario Bros. (NES)
Worst: Pinball (NES)

Super Mario Bros. is the easy one and it's still the right one. Everything after it was built out of pieces from this game.

Pinball is one table, one ball, no ramps, no multiball. You bump it around and then it drains. The bonus stage where Mario catches a girl on a trampoline is the most interesting thing in the cart, and it's a minigame.

What are your picks for 1985?

Best and Worst Games I own: 1987

Skipping 1986 since the only game from that year I have is Popeye, and I already gave that one a positive review. 

Best: The Legend of Zelda (NES) 
Worst: Ikari Warriors (NES)

Zelda doesn't explain anything to you. Sword, field, go. Nobody had a map, everybody had a theory, and most of them were wrong.

Ikari Warriors is what happens when an arcade game with a rotary stick gets put on a d-pad. One hit and you're done. Without the continue code I don't think anyone was seeing the end of it.

What's your best and worst of 1987?

Best and Worst Games I own: 1988

Best: Contra (NES)
Worst: Rambo (NES)

Super Mario Bros. 2 and Zelda II both came out in 1988 and neither one is the pick. Thirty seconds into the first stage of Contra you know exactly how good you are.

Rambo is a movie about a guy with a machine gun turned into a game where you spend most of your time lost and talking to people.

What's your best and worst for 1988?

Best and Worst Games I own: 1989

Best: Tetris (NES)
Worst: Friday the 13th (NES)

I own several games from 1989 that could compete for the best, Mega Man 2 included, and Tetris still beats all of them. It's the one game from that year people who don't play games can sit down and play right now.

Friday the 13th puts you on the same brown trail between the same six cabins, throwing rocks at wolves and waiting on Jason. The game has little to do with the movie. 

What are your best and worst picks for 1989?

Best and Worst Games I own: 1990

Best: Batman The Video Game (NES)
Worst: Mad Max (NES)

Super Mario Bros. 3 came out in 1990 and I've already said plenty of times that it's the greatest game ever made, so I'm handing the 1990 crown over to a different game that came out right about the same time SMB3 did: Batman The Video Game.

Sunsoft didn't phone this one in the way most licensed games got phoned in. The wall jump is the whole game and it still feels right. The soundtrack is one of the best on the NES.

Mad Max is a top down driving game with the worst driving controls of all time. You hunt for gas and ammo in an empty desert and there's no clear objective. I don't remember how I ended up with this one when I was a kid.

What are your best and worst picks for 1990?

Best and Worst Games I own: 1991

Best: Super Mario World (SNES)
Worst: Bill & Ted's Excellent Video Game Adventure (NES)

Sonic the Hedgehog and Streets of Rage both came out this year. Unfortunately for them, Super Mario World also came out this year. This is the game that came with our SNES, and the one my mom and I spent the most time playing together. 35 years later and this game still has infinite replayability.

Bill & Ted has some of the most annoying music ever put in a game, and that alone is enough to make it the worst thing I own from 1991. The rest of the game doesn't help it.

What are your best and worst picks for 1991?

best_worst.intro:
Best and Worst Games I own: 1992

Best: Street Fighter II (SNES)
Worst: The Great Waldo Search (NES)

Hardest pick I've had to make in this series. 

Super Mario Kart, Sonic the Hedgehog 2, Super Star Wars and Golden Axe II all came out in 1992. 

Street Fighter II still beats every one of them.

The Great Waldo Search is a book you already owned sold to you again for fifty dollars. You drag a magnifying glass across a still picture on a timer, four times, and that's the game.

What are your best and worst picks for 1992?

Best and Worst Games I own: 1993

Best: Street Fighter II Turbo (SNES)
Worst: Mario is Missing! (SNES)

Not only is Turbo the best Street Fighter ever made, it's also the best fighting game ever made. This is the version where Capcom put it all together on the SNES. You finally got playable bosses and mirror matches at home, and the speed setting turned it into a different game than the one that came out the year before.

1993 is one of the best years in gaming history.

Mortal Kombat, Secret of Mana, Star Fox, Jungle Strike all came out that year and Street Fighter II Turbo is better than all of them.

One of the worst games not only of 1993, but of all time, is Mario is Missing! You walk around as Luigi asking people geography questions. It has Mario's name on it but this is in no way an actual Mario game. Nintendo put their name on it too, and what you actually got was a school assignment somebody charged full price for.

What are your best and worst picks for 1993?

Best and Worst Games I own: 1994

Best: Spider-Man & Venom: Maximum Carnage (SNES)
Worst: Rise of the Robots (SNES)

1994 was a stacked year for games. Quality title after quality title came out that year.

Super Street Fighter II, Sonic the Hedgehog 3, Mortal Kombat II, Earthworm Jim and Final Fantasy III all came out in 1994.

My mom rented Maximum Carnage from Blockbuster for me in 1994. I loved it. I also couldn't beat it, and it stayed that way until I played the Marvel MaXimum Collection on Xbox recently and finally got through it. It sits at No. 5 on my top 10 beat em ups and No. 6 on my top 10 superhero games.

Rise of the Robots had one of the biggest marketing campaigns of the 90s only for it to be a dud of a game. I bought this game recently and it's really not a good game at all. The controls are terrible and the game is just flat out boring. The only bright spot of this game is Brian May from Queen did the music.

What are your best and worst picks for 1994?

Best and Worst Games I own: 1995

Best: Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island (SNES)
Worst: Batman Forever (SNES)

Yoshi's Island is one of my all-time favorite games and the first game I ever finished on my own as a kid. The gameplay and the artwork are what make this game so great. The game is a perfect game.

1995 itself was packed with incredible games:

Killer Instinct
Mortal Kombat 3
Virtua Fighter 2
NBA Jam TE
Separation Anxiety
Batman & Robin

Batman Forever showed up three months after the movie and Acclaim built it with digitized actors that made it look like a Mortal Kombat ripoff turned into a side scroller. It was weird and out of place. The gameplay was dreadfully bad.

Batman Forever is one of my favorite movies and to me, it's the ultimate 90s movie. The marketing for it was insane, it was everywhere, and I still have one of the frosted glass mugs from McDonald's.

Now imagine how disappointed I was with this being the game we got. What a huge letdown.

What are your best and worst picks for 1995?

Best and Worst Games I own: 1996

Best: Wave Race 64 (Nintendo 64)
Worst: NBA Jam Extreme (PlayStation)

Super Mario 64 released as a launch title for the N64 and it's the game most people would pick as the best for 1996. I've said multiple times on here where I stand: Mario 64 is an important piece in gaming history. It hasn't aged well. The constant battle with the camera ruins the game.
 
Wave Race on the other hand, this is what a perfect game looks like and one that has infinite replay value, even 30 years after its release. The game physics are really something else for 1996. The water moves differently every time you run a course, so you aren't memorizing turns the way you do in almost every racing game made since.

1996 was deep too. Tomb Raider, Twisted Metal 2, Pilotwings 64, Killer Instinct Gold all came out that year.

NBA Jam Extreme wasn't a terrible game, but what Acclaim did with it was a downgrade from the previous entries in the series. Replacing Tim Kitzrow with Marv Albert as the announcer was a terrible move.

What are your picks for 1996?

Best and Worst Games I own: 1997

Best: GoldenEye 007 (Nintendo 64)
Worst: Madden Football 64 (Nintendo 64)

1997 is one of the most iconic years in video game history and easily the best year of the 90s.

Star Fox 64, Diddy Kong Racing, Mario Kart 64, Extreme-G and Final Fantasy VII all released in 1997.

GoldenEye was an event every weekend. Kids in our neighborhood would come over and we'd spend hours on four player multiplayer.

I remember renting Madden 64 from Blockbuster and being so confused. It didn't have the NFL license that year because Acclaim had it locked up for the N64 that season, so EA shipped a Madden game with no team names, no logos and no team colors. The Pro Bowl is called the Madden Bowl in it. The Super Bowl is the EAS Championship.

What are your picks for 1997?

Best and Worst Games I own: 1998

Best: Metal Gear Solid (PlayStation)
Worst: Batman & Robin (PlayStation)

1998 is the year people point at when they argue gaming peaked, usually meaning Ocarina of Time. 

I'd take Metal Gear Solid over it. 

Batman & Robin was originally supposed to release alongside the movie in 1997 but the game was nowhere near completion, so it got delayed a year. 

The delay didn't help as this game still turned out bad.

What are your picks for 1998?

Best and Worst Games I own: 1999

Best: Star Wars Episode I: Racer (Nintendo 64)
Worst: Superman: The New Superman Adventures (Nintendo 64)

1999 had Donkey Kong 64, Syphon Filter, Final Fantasy VIII, Gran Turismo 2, Marvel Super Heroes vs. Street Fighter and WWF WrestleMania 2000.

Star Wars Episode I: Racer gets the spot over all of them.

My brother borrowed this one from a friend of his. I took it over and played it nonstop until the kid wanted it back. It's the best Star Wars game ever made, third on my all time N64 games list ahead of Super Mario 64 and Ocarina of Time.

Superman 64 is the worst game ever made. Nothing further needs to be said about it. Just an awful game.

What are you picks for 1999?

Best and Worst Games I own: 2000

Best: Perfect Dark (Nintendo 64)
Worst: Q*bert (Game Boy Color)

2000 had Majora's Mask, WWF No Mercy, Syphon Filter 2, Mega Man Legends 2, Shenmue, Crazy Taxi and Street Fighter III: Double Impact.

Perfect Dark gets the spot over all of them. It's the game GoldenEye should have been, second on my all time Nintendo 64 list right behind Wave Race 64.

Q*bert on the Game Boy Color is the arcade game squeezed onto a screen too small for it. Half the time you can't tell which way you're about to jump until you've already gone off the edge of the pyramid.

What are your picks for 2000?

head_to_head.intro:
Super Mario Bros. 3 or Super Mario World?

My parents got me Mario 3 for my birthday in 1990. My mom and I played it constantly until we beat it. My dad would stay up late on weekends playing it with me too, and he's not even close to being a gamer.

Super Mario World came with our SNES a few years later and my mom and I did the same thing all over again.

Both games come with a lot of great memories, but I still think 3 is the better game.

Which one are you taking?
head_to_head.quote: Both games come with a lot of great memories, but I still think 3 is the better game.

head_to_head.intro:
Ocarina of Time or Majora's Mask?

I remember playing Ocarina of Time after it got released in 1998. We rented it from Blockbuster and ended up holding onto it for a full week. This game was nothing short of impressive. Link running around in a 3D open world was incredible, but eventually it got boring.

A couple of years later Majora's Mask came out and I found it to be way more entertaining. Same engine, but a much darker game. The moon in this game was straight up nightmare fuel.

Which Zelda game on the Nintendo 64 did you like more?
head_to_head.quote: A couple of years later Majora's Mask came out and I found it to be way more entertaining.

head_to_head.intro:
Two carts. Pick your side.

Ocarina of Time is the one everybody names first. The default answer. The one you're supposed to say.

Majora's Mask is the weird one. Three days. Falling moon. The dread that never lets up.

Gray cart is everyone's answer. Gold cart is the right one.
head_to_head.quote: Gray cart is everyone's answer. Gold cart is the right one.

head_to_head.intro:
Mario Kart 64 or Diddy Kong Racing?

We owned Mario Kart 64 as kids and played it constantly. We were always team Mario in my house. I didn't get around to playing Diddy Kong Racing until a few years ago and it didn't take long to realize it was the better game.

Which one did you put more hours into?
head_to_head.quote: I didn't get around to playing Diddy Kong Racing until a few years ago and it didn't take long to realize it was the better game.

head_to_head.intro:
Perfect Dark or GoldenEye?

GoldenEye is the one everybody remembers, and it earned that. It has a permanent spot in 90s pop culture history. 

Kids in my neighborhood would come over on a Saturday and we'd spend hours on four player multiplayer.

Perfect Dark came out 3 years later and it quickly became the better game.

Who's taking GoldenEye over Perfect Dark?
head_to_head.quote: Perfect Dark came out 3 years later and it quickly became the better game.

head_to_head.intro:
Streets of Rage 2 or Turtles in Time?

We were strictly a Nintendo house growing up. No Genesis, so Turtles in Time is the one I actually put hours into.

I didn't play Streets of Rage 2 until years later and I still think Turtles in Time is the better game.

What was your beat em up growing up?
head_to_head.quote: I didn't play Streets of Rage 2 until years later and I still think Turtles in Time is the better game.

head_to_head.intro:
Mortal Kombat II or Killer Instinct?

Killer Instinct was supposed to be the Mortal Kombat killer. It got a sequel on the N64 and then Rare was done with it.

MKII is number two on my all time fighting games list. Killer Instinct is number nine.

Which one was the better fighting game?
head_to_head.quote: MKII is number two on my all time fighting games list. Killer Instinct is number nine.

head_to_head.intro:
Killer Instinct or Primal Rage?

Primal Rage came out on the Super Nintendo on this day in 1995. Killer Instinct landed five days later on August 30.

Killer Instinct is the better game and I don't think that's up for debate. Rare's prerendered sprites, the combo system, the soundtrack CD in the box.

Primal Rage is my guilty pleasure. The reviews were rough and I'm not going to argue with any of it. Clay dinosaurs shot frame by frame, fatalities where they eat the little people cheering at the bottom of the screen. It's not a great game but it's absolutely a fun game.

Which 1995 fighter did you like more?
head_to_head.quote: Killer Instinct is the better game and I don't think that's up for debate.

posts.text:
Super Mario Galaxy and Odyssey are the most overrated games Nintendo ever made. I quit Galaxy in under an hour and finally gave up on Odyssey about halfway through.
 
Then Super Mario Wonder comes out and reminds you what a Mario game is supposed to feel like. Tight, inventive, fun from the first jump. I didn't want to put it down.
 
Super Mario World did it in 1990. Wonder did it in 2023. The 3D games keep chasing spectacle and forgetting the part where it's fun.

The best 2D Mario beats anything they've made in 3D. Not close.
